native_dataflow: Every run reads one full 128x512 I8 matrix, returns128 complete rows and takes one input vector. Per expert/chip there is exactly one executed run. Host scatters rows; no partial sums, coding, quantization or new accumulator type. GU->host activation->down dependency is retained.
software_required: Controller stores/follows tile owner and row-offset maps, matches currently selected six experts to four omission choices and dispatches existing block/offset/page-count GEMVs. The published host aif_post does not directly expose these addresses. No new die PE is used.
numeric_scope: 236 structural expert/omit maps independently checked. The generator also ran synthetic INT64 reference GEMVs. Neither demonstrates a physical AiF result datatype or real model inference; full-row copies preserve the original per-row arithmetic instead of introducing a new type.
capacity: The43MiB extra are useful/physical-page I8 payload. In this standalone phase all90-92 atoms/chip fit one192-wave block stripe; block reservation is192MiB including idle tails. Other model streams may share those tails. Do not equate page storage optimality with reserved-stripe optimality. Scale arrays, FTL/ECC/spare and other tensors are excluded.
timing_limit: 166912ns is an arithmetic model, not measured latency: it omits route-matcher/controller lookup work and host reassembly/activation compute. The72-command and transfer costs are explicit; tR28us/control250ns/host2us remain uncalibrated assumptions. No background/erase, q-replay or request SLO claim.

byte_bound_extension.proof: Let u_ec be logical weight bytes of expert e that have exactly one stored copy, on chip c. For every6-expert route S, native distinct-input GEMVs require at least sum_e_in_S ceil(u_ec/65536) waves on c. Thus at most five experts can have u_ec>0. A route containing all of those experts plus arbitrary others gives sum_e ceil(u_ec/65536)<=5, hence sum_e u_ec<=5W. Across16chips U<=80W. With logical bytes B=768W and no cross-item dedup or coding, stored useful bytes >=U+2(B-U)=2B-U, so extra>=688W. Construction attains that byte count without row fragmentation or padding.
requirements: down experts have independent input contexts per ordinary NAND wave
no read-once/PB replay across those contexts or independent per-plane contexts
no dense block-diagonal zero embedding with concatenated expert inputs
all necessary weights stored on device; no host weight computation/cache shortcut
no coding or physical dedup across distinct logical weight items
byte_bound_extension.exclusions: GU common-input row packing is not covered by sum-per-expert ceil. Neither are block-diagonal multi-expert dense matrices, altered cache/compute interfaces or cross-item representations. The byte bound is about copies, not erase-block tails. Do not claim unrestricted arbitrary-row optimality from this conditional lemma.

existing_hardware_counterexample.embedding: diag(W_A,W_B) has64rows x1024columns with32768bytes useful weights and32768bytes structural zeros; concatenate x_A and x_B.
existing_hardware_counterexample.violates: sum_e ceil(u_ec/W) as an unrestricted hardware lower bound
existing_hardware_counterexample.canonical_scope: Two whole128x512 canonical tiles instead produce a256x1024 block diagonal matrix,256KiB/fourwaves versus original two full waves. This fringe counterexample does not refute the audited canonical tile construction.

novelty_assessment: Not established. The construction uses standard replicated declustering plus a mandatory singleton-byte counting lower bound and a four-color Hall matching. The exact compound-query parameter point is validated, but these ingredients look like a short corollary of existing replicated/batch-code theory. A full primary literature check is needed before claiming a new theorem, and this alone is not an architecture breakthrough.
